script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A young, DISHEVELLED MAN sits on a bench, looking at himself in a mirror. He runs a hand through his unkempt beard and sighs.

DISHEVELLED MAN
(muttering to himself)
Who am I?

The mirror reflects not his face, but the faces of various strangers passing by.

EXT. CITY PARK - BENCH - CONTINUOUS

The Dishevelled Man, now dressed in a sharp suit, sits across from a PSYCHOLOGIST, DR. ROBERTS.

DR. ROBERTS
You seem preoccupied with the question of your identity.

DISHEVELLED MAN
I don't know who I am. I feel like I've lost myself.

DR. ROBERTS
Tell me about your childhood. What memories stand out to you?

DISHEVELLED MAN
(thinking)
I remember my parents arguing a lot. My dad was always working, and my mom was always unhappy. I didn't have many friends growing up. I was always the odd one out.

DR. ROBERTS
And how did you cope with that feeling of isolation?

Dishevelled Man hesitates before answering.

DISHEVELLED MAN
I tried to fit in. I pretended to be someone I wasn't. I wore the right clothes, said the right things, but it never felt genuine.

DR. ROBERTS
(nods)
So, you've spent your life trying to be someone you're not. But what if I told you that everyone does that to some extent?

EXT. CITY PARK - BENCH - LATER

The Dishevelled Man sits on the bench, staring at a group of children playing nearby. He watches as they laugh and play, and a small smile forms on his lips.

DISHEVELLED MAN
(to himself)
Maybe I don't have to be someone I'm not. Maybe it's okay to just be myself.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The Dishevelled Man, now clean-shaven and dressed casually, sits across from an old FRIEND, LUCY.

LUCY
(surprised)
Wow, you look great! What's new?

DISHEVELLED MAN
I've been thinking a lot about who I am and what I want out of life. I've realized that I don't have to be the person everyone expects me to be.

LUCY
(smiling)
That's great to hear. I've always thought you were a unique and interesting person.

Dishevelled Man smiles back at her.

DISHEVELLED MAN
Thanks, Lucy. It's nice to hear that from someone who knew me before I tried to fit in.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

The Dishevelled Man sits on the bench, looking at the lake. He closes his eyes and takes a deep breath. A woman, MRS. JENKINS, approaches and sits down next to him.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
You look like you're deep in thought.

DISHEVELLED MAN
(startled)
Yes, I am. I've been thinking about who I am and what I want out of life.

MRS. JENKINS
(nods)
It's never too late to figure that out. And sometimes, all it takes is a little introspection.

Dishevelled Man nods, and they sit in silence for a moment.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY - LATER

The Dishevelled Man stands up and walks away from the bench, a sense of purpose in his step. He looks back at the lake one last time before disappearing into the crowd.

FADE OUT.

THE END
